name: ioc-rats-rootkits
description: RAT / backdoor / rootkit indicators (Reptile, Diamorphine & other LKM rootkits, BPFDoor, XorDDoS, RotaJakiro, Skidmap, RedXOR/Winnti, HiddenWasp). Present == investigate.  Absent keys/paths SKIP, never false-fail.

rules.title: IOC: known LKM-rootkit module loaded
rules.rationale: These are the module names of public Linux kernel-mode rootkits (Diamorphine, Reptile, Adore-ng, KBeast, Suterusu, Cloud Snooper's snd_floppy…). A loaded one hides its own processes, files and network ports from you.  Cross-check with a trusted `lsmod` from rescue media — a good rootkit hides itself from the running kernel too.
rules.fix: If this indicator is unexpected, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the artifacts for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: reptile present (/reptile)
rules.rationale: The Reptile LKM rootkit installs into /reptile (reptile_cmd, reptile_shell). Its presence means an active kernel-mode compromise.
rules.fix: If you didn't put reptile there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: rc.modules present (/etc/rc.modules)
rules.rationale: Reptile and several LKM rootkits persist by loading their module from /etc/rc.modules.  Legitimate on a few old setups — confirm what it loads.
rules.fix: If you didn't put rc.modules there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: kdmtmpflush present (/dev/shm/kdmtmpflush)
rules.rationale: kdmtmpflush is a dropper/loader used by the BPFDoor passive backdoor, staged in shared memory to survive on disk-less.
rules.fix: If you didn't put kdmtmpflush there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: haldrund.pid present (/var/run/haldrund.pid)
rules.rationale: haldrund.pid is a lock file BPFDoor writes to ensure a single instance — a strong indicator of the BPFDoor implant.
rules.fix: If you didn't put haldrund.pid there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: gcc.sh present (/etc/cron.hourly/gcc.sh)
rules.rationale: gcc.sh in cron.hourly is XorDDoS's persistence stub — it re-drops the bot every hour.
rules.fix: If you didn't put gcc.sh there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: libudev.so present (/lib/libudev.so)
rules.rationale: XorDDoS ships a fake /lib/libudev.so (the real library is libudev.so.1 under the arch triplet dir). A bare /lib/libudev.so is a classic XorDDoS marker.  Confirm it isn't a legitimate dev symlink before acting.
rules.fix: If you didn't put libudev.so there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: systemd-daemon present (/lib/systemd/systemd-daemon)
rules.rationale: RotaJakiro masquerades as a systemd binary; there is no real 'systemd-daemon'. One of its documented persistence paths.
rules.fix: If you didn't put systemd-daemon there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: mozillat present (/usr/lib/mozillae/mozillat)
rules.rationale: A RotaJakiro payload path that impersonates Mozilla files.
rules.fix: If you didn't put mozillat there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: kaudited present (/usr/bin/kaudited)
rules.rationale: kaudited is a Skidmap component that installs malicious kernel modules and a fake 'pam' to backdoor authentication.
rules.fix: If you didn't put kaudited there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: pamdicks present (/usr/bin/pamdicks)
rules.rationale: pamdicks is a Skidmap payload used for persistence/credential theft.
rules.fix: If you didn't put pamdicks there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: iptabler present (/bin/iptabler)
rules.rationale: iptabler is a RedXOR (Winnti-linked) backdoor component that mimics the iptables name.
rules.fix: If you didn't put iptabler there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.

rules.title: IOC: .ifup-local present (/sbin/.ifup-local)
rules.rationale: A dot-hidden network hook script is HiddenWasp-style persistence — legit ifup-local is never hidden.  A visible /sbin/ifup-local can be a normal admin hook; the hidden dot-file is not.
rules.fix: If you didn't put .ifup-local there deliberately, treat the host as possibly compromised: isolate it, capture the file for analysis, and hunt for persistence.
